Search & Notifications

Spec §9's final row. ClickUp is out — you declined it, and the spec always said "if still wanted". Plan file: docs/plans/2026-08-25-phase-6-polish.md

Grounded on measurement, not assumption. 1.2 GB of transcripts (773 MB Claude + 429 MB Codex). A phrase search across the whole Claude corpus with plain grep: 124 ms from the shell — but the number that matters is the path the feature takes: ~460 ms end-to-end through Node for a 1,046-file match (the grep is ~34 ms; the rest is Node's spawn overhead). Corrected during Task 1 by review; the conclusion is unchanged. That number is why this phase needs no index, no dependency, and no FTS table — and it disproves a comment phase 3 left behind saying full-text "would need an index MM does not keep". Part of Task 4 is correcting that comment.

  • Two steps, no new reader. grep answers "which files", the phase-1/2 parsers answer "what does it say". MM never grows a second way to read a transcript.
  • Synthetic messages stay excluded — command wrappers, task notifications, Codex machine blocks. They are not things you wrote or read, and phase 2 already settled that rule.
  • A grep hit with no snippet is normal, not an error: the raw JSON matched but the parser classified the event as synthetic. Those hits are dropped.
  • It lives in History, behind a "search inside sessions" toggle. Off is today's instant card filter, untouched.
Notifications — pure web, transition-only core
  • No server change at all. A hook over the feed useSessions already provides.
  • Fires on the transition into needs_you, never on a sustained one — the feed re-broadcasts every ~500 ms and would otherwise notify forever.
  • A fresh page load never notifies for state that already existed. This is the case most likely to be got wrong, so it gets its own test and a teeth-check.
  • Permission is requested on your click, because browsers ignore it otherwise. If the browser has no Notification API the toggle is hidden rather than dead.
The trade-off you chose: browser notifications only fire while a board tab is open. The alternative — the server spawning osascript — works with no browser but means MM's daemon interrupts you from the background. You picked the quieter one.

Risks the plan pre-empts review
  • grep exit 1 means "no match", not failure — treating it as an error makes every empty search look broken.
  • Regex injection — -F makes your "(" literal; -- stops a query starting with "-" being read as a flag. Phase 4 learned that one the hard way with codex exec. Both get a pinning test.
  • Notification spam — transition-only, and never on reload.
  • Cadence check — Tasks 1–3 touch server/src, so server.test.ts runs at the real 5 s / 500 ms cadence before merge. --config /dev/null is not that check: it silently drops the web tests.

ClickUp export: dropped per your instruction. Nothing in this phase sends anything anywhere.
